nodes.label: Next.js agent rules
nodes.rationale: The repository's Next.js version has breaking changes, so relevant local documentation and deprecation notices must be consulted before writing code.

nodes.label: Single-QR ordering app
nodes.rationale: One shared QR link is used for the restaurant menu, while customer identity and table details are entered manually rather than encoded in the QR.

nodes.label: Customer identity and table input
nodes.rationale: Customers type their name, WhatsApp number, and table number by hand; those values are not encoded in the QR.

nodes.label: Role-scoped dashboards
nodes.rationale: Kitchen, cashier, and admin dashboards expose separate internal workflows and are protected by role.

nodes.label: Role-gated access
nodes.rationale: Internal dashboards are restricted to the staff role that owns each workflow.

nodes.label: English-only internal dashboards
nodes.rationale: Staff dashboards are internal tools rather than customer-facing surfaces, so they do not carry the customer i18n provider.

nodes.label: Row-level security policies
nodes.rationale: Database permissions and policies enforce authorization independently of the user interface.

nodes.label: public.profiles
nodes.rationale: Staff roles are stored in profiles and users cannot write their own role column, preventing a self-escalation path.

nodes.label: profiles RLS policy
nodes.rationale: Role assignment for existing accounts uses normal profiles RLS rather than a privileged application route.

nodes.label: create_order()
nodes.rationale: This is the only order write path and it re-prices each line item server-side so a tampered client payload cannot change totals.

nodes.label: Order status transitions
nodes.rationale: Status transitions are enforced in Postgres rather than only in the UI, with role-specific gates.

nodes.label: set_item_availability()
nodes.rationale: Cashiers can change item availability only through this function and cannot edit prices, photos, or names through a direct table grant.

nodes.label: Customer PII
nodes.rationale: Customer name and WhatsApp number are excluded from anonymous order access while staff retain full-row visibility.

nodes.label: Anonymous orders column grant
nodes.rationale: Anonymous customers receive only the fields needed by the live tracker: order identity, table, status, total, and timestamps.

nodes.label: Order ratings
nodes.rationale: Ratings are limited to one submission per order and only become valid after the order is closed.

nodes.label: public.security_events
nodes.rationale: Role changes are audited automatically without copying personally identifying information into the security event record.

nodes.label: Failed login attempts
nodes.rationale: Failed attempts are not duplicated in the application's database because Supabase Auth already records them and verifies passwords itself.

nodes.label: Service-role key exclusion
nodes.rationale: The application keeps privileged Supabase service credentials and privileged API routes out of the app.

nodes.label: First-admin bootstrap
nodes.rationale: Creating the first admin is deliberately a one-time dashboard and SQL-editor operation rather than an application feature.

nodes.label: Leaked-password protection
nodes.rationale: HaveIBeenPwned password checks are a Supabase Auth project setting and are not reachable through SQL migrations.

nodes.label: Live Supabase project verification
nodes.rationale: Completed phases were verified against the deployed Supabase project with real orders, role logins, and end-to-end Realtime propagation.
